title: Is resistance ever free? Weighing the costs of altered strigolactone biosynthesis in sorghum
content: Strigolactones were first identified as germination stimulants for the parasitic plant Striga spp. (Cook et al. 1966), establishing a direct link between these carotenoid-derived hormones and parasite infestation. Striga hermonthica is a major constraint to cereal production and food security in tropical Africa, where it parasitizes several cereal crops, including sorghum, maize, and rice, causing billions of dollars of crop damage each year (Spallek et al. 2013). The susceptibility of sorghum, a globally important C4 cereal, is closely linked to its root-exuded strigolactones, and natural variation in these compounds.
